newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Tractebel unit buys into French Geostock.
newsitem.headline: Tractebel unit buys into French Geostock.

text.p: Tractebel Engineering, a unit of Belgian multinational utility Tractebel, has bought a 25 percent stake in French engineering firm Geostock, Tractebel said in a statement on Monday.
It gave no financial details of the deal.
The other shareholders of Geostock, each with a 25 percent stake, are Elf Aquitaine, Total and BP France, Tractebel said.
Geostock, a world leader in underground storage of hydrocarbons, has an annual turnover equivalent to 840 million Belgian francs of which 20 percent comes from outside France, the statement said.
Its core activities include the design, building and operation of underground storage facilities, and also services for the treatment and rehabilitation of polluted soil.

"This purchase further broadens the Tractebel Engineering know-how concerning gas storage and offers new international development opportunities for the Tractebel Group's business units active in the field of gas," the statement said.
